candidate.title: BruDRB-seq
candidate.scope: BruDRB-seq middle-row schematic from the assigned Illumina poster: DRB inhibition and release, analog labeling of nascent RNA, isolation/hydrolysis, antibody-bead enrichment, elution/end preparation, and cDNA production. The separately labeled upper 5′-GRO-seq and lower 4sUDRB-seq rows, and the partial chemical drawing at far right, are visible neighboring context, not alternative targets of this BruDRB-seq card. No arrows connect those rows to this route. The matching collection page explicitly captions its middle-row reproduction as BruDRB-seq. The primary-paper in-cell bromouridine implementation resolves the misleading run-on/Br-UTP wording; the remaining diagram-specific preparation blocks are retained at schematic scope.

operations.label: Transient inhibition of initiated RNAPII
operations.description: Apply DRB to cells containing RNAPII and nascent RNA, producing a drug-treated population restrained at the initiation/promoter-proximal stage before productive elongation.
operations.mechanism: Transient DRB-mediated inhibition of the transition into elongation; this does not stop already elongating polymerases.
operations.information_effect: Establishes the reversible starting perturbation for a synchronized advancing wave; continuing polymerases can also generate a receding wave.

operations.label: Synchronized run-on with analog
operations.description: Preserved diagram caption: the drawing shows Br-UTP star marks being incorporated into nascent RNA after DRB removal. In the primary-paper implementation used to interpret this record, cultured cells are supplied bromouridine (Bru), and newly transcribed RNA becomes Bru-labeled during transcriptional recovery.
operations.mechanism: In-cell nascent-RNA labeling with Bru in the primary implementation; the diagram’s run-on/Br-UTP wording is retained as an explicit discrepancy, not taken as evidence for an isolated-nucleus run-on.
operations.information_effect: Labels RNA synthesized during a defined recovery interval; it does not tag RNAPII itself or convert the DNA template into the measurement carrier.

operations.description: Convert the bead-associated RNA fraction into free labeled RNA fragments through the depicted elution and end-preparation block. The source caption additionally specifies cap removal and end repair; no finer internal reaction sequence or end-group outcome is asserted.

operations.label: Reverse transcription amplification
operations.description: Convert the prepared labeled RNA fraction into cDNA and amplify it to yield the depicted cDNA library.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription and amplification are a broad final block; the primary implementation identifies the Illumina TruSeq library kit without specifying its internal reactions here.
operations.information_effect: RNA-derived sequence is now carried by DNA. method_scopes.rationale: All seven operations belong to the independently captioned middle BruDRB-seq row. The left nascent-RNA cartoon illustrates the biological starting context and purpose, not another action. Its DRB-release and analog-immunocapture route matches the scope explicitly named by the collection page and Veloso et al. The primary implementation uses in-cell Bru labeling, not an inferred nuclear run-on. Cap removal/end repair and hydrolysis remain diagram-level claims; no neighboring 5′-GRO-seq adapter/kinase chemistry or 4sUDRB-seq biotin/streptavidin selection is imported.

corrections.diagram_observation: The BruDRB-seq row labels the analog Br-UTP and the synthesis step “Synchronized run-on with analog”; the matching secondary catalogue description likewise says Br-UTP is added after DRB removal.
corrections.primary_statement: Veloso et al. describe cultured cells recovering after DRB removal and being incubated in bromouridine-containing medium to label nascent RNA. Operation o3 and its output state s3 are authored using that in-cell Bru-labeling interpretation while retaining the literal drawing labels. The supplied primary evidence does not establish isolated nuclei or direct addition of Br-UTP as the assay implementation.

unknowns.question: Does the reported primary implementation use the exact depicted pre-capture hydrolysis and post-capture cap-removal/end-repair blocks? The supplied Methods report total-RNA isolation, antibody capture, and then TruSeq cDNA-library preparation without resolving these specific internal preparation steps. Explicit protocol text giving fragmentation and end-preparation order would resolve this implementation-level correspondence; the diagram-level route is retained.

checks.rationale: The correction preserves the visible Br-UTP legend and run-on caption while explicitly interpreting o3 and s3 using the matched BruDRB-seq paper. Results and Methods establish labeling of recovering cultured cells with bromouridine. The corrected cellular input s2, labeled cellular output s3, and subsequent isolation interface agree; no isolated-nucleus state or direct nucleotide-feeding mechanism is asserted. This is a resolved source discrepancy, not an unexplained impossibility.
